question: Whether f29v's same-carrier and written wet/dry order establish a temporal operation, and whether the two-part reading is independently supported.
assessment: No. GDT625 explicitly makes state order conditional on retaining one carrier; with a different or unknown carrier it remains a part contrast. Its corrected f29v reading assigns [otshy okaiin] and [cthy oltchy] to two carriers/parts, making parallel part-state phrases preferred locally over a time sequence, while drying remains secondary. This is a model preference grounded in the selected head/part bindings and opened-image judgment, not an independently confirmed temporal operation. GDT809 independently preserves the uncertainty: repeated okaiin does not establish one preparation, same batch, or direction; shol chol shol does not establish wet-dry-wet treatment; dry quality, dried state, and imperative to dry remain distinct claims.
duplicate_scope: This belongs with the existing CTHY/CHOR_SHOR quality-state failure/uncertainty scope and the GDT809 predecessor chain (GDT686/GDT764/GDT629). It should not become a new semantic success or rerun of the same contextual candidate ranking. The existing evidence supports a conditional state relation and unresolved subject/scope, not an operative temporal gloss.
reopen_condition: A genuinely new, independently bound carrier whose same referent is fixed before looking at state order, plus a held occurrence where a predeclared temporal operation predicts a state transition against the parallel-part/quality-state rival. Repeated wet/dry order, same spelling, or additional f29v readings alone are insufficient.

evidence.quote:
The first pass noticed `otshy ... oltchy` and read a possible cold-moist to
cold-dry transition. The local attachment is better:

```text
[otshy okaiin] [cthy oltchy]
[cold-moist <okaiin carrier>] [leaf drug: cold-dry]
```

Current German working line:

```text
<ysho>; kalt-feuchte Zubereitung/Charge; Blattgut kalt-trocken;
<s shot sho>; <okaiin>.
```

The drawing contains one plant but visibly different drug parts: flower,
buds/fruiting bodies, two large leaves and rootstock. That makes two parallel
part-state phrases more economical than a time sequence. Drying remains a
secondary reading, not the preferred one.

The all-form direction is essentially balanced. The exact-frame imbalance is
created mostly by adjacent dry/moist contrasts and cannot itself mean
"moisten." Written order therefore supplies a conditional relation, not an
automatic verb:

```text
same carrier + dry -> moist = befeuchten/einweichen
same carrier + moist -> dry = trocknen/abtrocknen lassen
different or unknown carrier = part contrast remains primary
```

Six successive three-state paths exist, and all are dry -> moist -> dry: two
KCH-KSH-KCH and four TCH-TSH-TCH. This is the shape expected for "soak, then
dry," but only f29v lies on an already opened image and that case splits more
cleanly into two carriers. The path remains a productive recipe template to
test, not a translation already won.

- `cthy chor shor` permits a plant-part or ingredient-list hypothesis. It does
  not identify the three organs or settle flower versus seed/fruit direction.
- `chor chol daiin` appears at both known locations in all three readings.
  Both descriptive degree syntax and recipe amount syntax remain possible.
- `daiin daiin` and two `chol chol` occurrences are left repeated. One
  `chol chol` occurrence has only two-reader support. Neither model may
  silently turn the repeats into one intensified state, six portions, or an
  invented second operation.
- `chocthy daiin cthaiin daiin` supplies two adjacent head/value-like fields
  in all three readings. The head identities and value axis remain open.
- `shol chol shol` does not by itself establish a wet-dry-wet treatment.
  The interpreted qualities or states still need subjects and scope.
- Repeated `okaiin` on f29v.4 establishes repeated spelling, not necessarily
  one preparation, the same batch, or a directional process.

At f32v.8, ZL3b/IT2a have `daiin [ctho daiin] qotaiin`, while RF1b has
`daiin [cthodaiin] qotaiin`. The matched inner character sequence motivates
a local word-boundary alternative. It does not identify `ctho`, export a
`cth` root, or establish that spaces are generally optional.

Historical comparison adds a useful distinction: dry as a constitutional
quality, dried as a material state, and an imperative to dry are different
claims. The primary comparators and their dates/access limits are documented
in [the historical review](src/HISTORICAL_PASSAGE_REVIEW.md). Historical
compatibility is not a Voynich-to-Latin dictionary match.
